data.text:
As per a traffic advisory, lane-wise traffic on the Chandmari Flyover will be stopped on an alternate basis from the evening of January 24.

Each lane will remain closed for 15 days, resulting in a total construction period of 30 days. 

For vehicles coming from the Zoo Road side, commuters are advised to proceed towards Rajgarh Road via Apurba Sinha Path or directly through Rajgarh Road. 

From Rajgarh Road, alternative routes include South Sarania Road, G.S. Road, Dr. B. Baruah Road and G.N.B. Road.

Vehicles approaching from the Chandmari side should proceed towards Bamunimaidam via M.R.D. Road. 

From M.R.D. Road, vehicles may continue towards Hatigarh Chariali via Railway Colony Road or take the Noonmati–Mathgharia route.

Meanwhile, all city buses have been strictly instructed to maintain lane discipline by operating only on the left-most lane and refraining from overtaking to reduce congestion at Chandmari. 

The advisory also refers to an RTA Board meeting held on October 13, 2025, which mandated left-most lane driving by city buses throughout their journey. 

Overtaking and left-side overtaking by diesel-fuelled city buses operating on the same route have been strictly prohibited.

Authorities have appealed to the public to cooperate during the period of traffic restrictions.
